issues.title: Let people share dishes, menus and places
issues.body:
Add a Share button so people can send a dish, a dining hall's menu or a place to friends, for example "J2 has queso tonight 👀" with a link that opens straight to it.

## What can be shared
- **A dish**: name, location, meal and date, with dietary tags. Opens the dish's detail (nutrition, allergens).
- **A menu**: a location's menu for a date and meal ("Kins dinner, Fri Nov 28"). Opens that menu.
- **A place**: any location (dining hall, café, restaurant, food truck) with hours and open-now status. Opens the place's page, or its pin on the map.
- Later: a meal plan or a favorites list, once those can be shown to someone without an account.

## How it works
- Share button in the dish sheet, the menu header and the place page, plus a long-press "Share" action on dish rows. Uses the native iOS share sheet (`Share` / `expo-sharing`), with a short message and the link.
- Links use `https://utdining.app/...` paths, for example `/dish/<id>?date=2026-11-28&meal=dinner`, `/menu/<location>?date=…&meal=…`, `/place/<location>`.
- **Universal links**: with the app installed, the link opens the right screen in the app. Needs an `apple-app-site-association` file on utdining.app (served by the website app) and `associatedDomains` in the Expo config, plus routing in expo-router for each path.
- **Website fallback**: without the app, the same URL renders a simple read-only page on the website (dish, menu or place) with an "Open in the App Store" banner (Smart App Banner meta tag).
- Links never break: if the dish or menu is gone (old date, menu not posted), show the location's current menu with a short note instead of an error.

## Link preview image
- Dynamic Open Graph images per link with Next.js `ImageResponse` (`opengraph-image.tsx`): dish name, location, meal and date, dietary icons, and the UT Dining brand, in the app's typography. Places show the place photo, name and today's hours.
- Set `og:title`, `og:description` and `twitter:card=summary_large_image` so iMessage, Instagram DMs, Discord and X show a rich card.
- Cache the images (they change only when the menu does) to stay within Vercel Hobby limits.

## Technical notes
- Dish ids must be stable enough to link to across scrapes; if they aren't, link by location + date + meal + dish name slug and resolve on open.
- Website pages read Supabase with the anon key only, and are indexable like the public status page.
- Analytics: log share taps and link opens (type only, no message content).
- Times and dates in Central time.

## Done when
- Dishes, menus and places can be shared from the app with the native share sheet.
- Tapping a link opens the right screen in the app when installed, and a working web page otherwise.
- Links show a branded preview image in iMessage and other common apps.

issues.title: Add a public read-only MCP server for UT Dining data

labels.name: backend
labels.description: Supabase, edge functions, scraper or shared DB package

issues.body:
Publish a public, read-only MCP server so people can add UT Dining as a custom connector in Claude or ChatGPT and ask things like "what's vegan at J2 tonight?" or "what's open near Gregory Gym after 10?".

This is a power-user and launch-buzz feature, not core app work. It should stay small and cost nothing to run.

## Tools to expose
- **`get_menu`**: menu for a location, date and meal (defaults to today and the current meal), with dish names, categories, allergens and dietary tags.
- **`search_dishes`**: find dishes by name or dietary filter (vegan, vegetarian, gluten free, allergen free) across locations for a date range.
- **`get_nutrition`**: nutrition facts for a dish (calories, macros, serving size, ingredients when available).
- **`list_locations`**: places with type, address, coordinates, payment methods and whether each is open now.
- **`get_hours`**: hours for a location for a date or the week, in Central time.

All tools are read-only. No accounts, favorites, meal plans or anything personal.

## Hosting
- A route on the existing Next.js website on Vercel (Hobby), e.g. `utdining.app/api/mcp`, using the Streamable HTTP transport (stateless, no sessions).
- Reads Supabase with the public anon key only, through the same RLS the app uses. No service key in this route.
- Cache responses: menus and hours change at most a few times a day, so cache per (tool, args) with `s-maxage` / Next data cache for 15–60 minutes and revalidate after the scraper runs.
- Return compact JSON (trim unused columns) to keep tokens and egress small.

## Cost and risks
- Expected cost is about $0: the user's own AI does the reasoning, and we only serve cached reads.
- **Vercel function limits**: Hobby caps invocations, duration and bandwidth. Caching plus short responses should keep it well under. Add a per-IP rate limit (Vercel firewall rule or middleware) so one misbehaving client can't burn the quota.
- **Supabase egress**: the free tier egress cap is shared with the app. Caching means Supabase is hit roughly once per cache window per query shape, not per request. Watch usage after launch.
- Abuse is limited to reading public menu data, which is already on UT's site.

## Docs and launch
- A short page on the website ("Use UT Dining in Claude / ChatGPT") with the connector URL and setup steps for each client, plus example prompts.
- Mention it in the 2.0 launch posts.

## Done when
- Adding the URL as a custom connector works in Claude and ChatGPT, and the five tools return correct data for today.
- Responses are cached, rate limited, and use only the anon key.
- The website has a setup page for the connector.

issues.title: Add a For You page with personal picks
issues.body:
Add a "For You" screen that pulls together what's most useful to each person right now, in one place.

## Sections
- **Your favorites today**: favorited dishes on today's menus, with location and meal. Shares matching with #114 (favorite alerts) and #121 (upcoming favorites preview, which can supply a "Coming up this week" row).
- **Open near you, closing soon**: open places sorted by distance, with closes-soon badges from #119.
- **New and trending**: dishes that haven't appeared in the last few weeks ("New at Kins"), and later the top-rated dishes today from #116 (dish ratings).
- **Picks for you**: dishes similar to your favorites and to items you've added to the meal plan, filtered by the allergen and dietary profile from #120 (matching items hidden or flagged).

Empty sections are hidden. If nothing applies (new user, no favorites), show a short prompt to favorite a few dishes and set dietary preferences.

## MVP (on-device, no account)
- Built entirely from data already on the phone: today's menus in SQLite, favorites, meal plan history, location hours, and the allergen profile.
- "Picks for you" starts simple: same dish name at other locations, dishes sharing the main words of favorited names, and dishes from the halls you favorite most. No ML.
- "New" = dish name not seen at that location in the last 21 days, which needs the app to keep a small local history of seen menu items (name, location, last seen date).
- Location sorting only with location permission; otherwise use favorite halls.

## Technical notes
- New tab or a section at the top of Home; decide in design. Keep it fast: compute in a single query/hook (`useForYou`) and cache for the current meal period.
- Everything in Central time; refresh when the meal period changes.
- Nothing personal leaves the device in the MVP. Analytics may log section taps (no dish names tied to allergen info).
- Server-side ratings/trending only arrive once #116 exists; the section hides until then.

## Done when
- For You shows favorites today, open-and-closing-soon places, new dishes, and picks, each hidden when empty.
- Allergen profile rules apply to every section.
- Works offline from cached data.

labels.name: backend
labels.description: Supabase, edge functions, scraper or shared DB package

issues.body:
Let people report wrong hours, menus or location info from inside the app, and route it to the same place as automated data checks.

## Scope
- **"Report wrong info"** on each location page and food detail screen.
- Short form: what's wrong (hours, menu, closed/open, location/photo, other), optional note (280 chars), optional screenshot later.
- Confirmation: "Thanks, we'll check it."
- No account needed.

## Technical notes
- **Supabase table** `data_reports`: id, location_id, food name (optional), kind enum, note, app version, device_id, created_at, status (`open` | `resolved` | `dismissed`). Insert-only for anon via RLS; reads only for dashboard admins (existing admin allowlist).
- **Abuse limits**: insert through an RPC or Edge Function that rate-limits per device (for example 5 per hour, 20 per day), trims and length-checks the note, and drops exact duplicates. No free text is ever shown publicly.
- **Dashboard view**: a Reports page listing open reports grouped by location, with the location's current hours side by side, and resolve/dismiss actions.
- **Feed the health check**: the scraper's places-health step (`scripts/ci/health-issue.sh`, `places-health` label) should include open user reports in the health issue, for example "J2: 3 users reported wrong hours in the last 24 h". Optionally trigger the issue when one location gets 3+ reports in a day.
- Privacy policy: mention that reports store an anonymous device id and app version.

## Done when
- A report can be sent from a location and a dish, and shows in the dashboard.
- Rate limits reject spam without breaking normal use.
- Open reports appear in the places-health issue.

issues.title: Show offline and last-synced banners for stale menus
issues.body:
Make it obvious when the app is showing old data, so yesterday's cached menu isn't mistaken for today's.

## Today
The app keeps menus in SQLite and tracks `lastSupabaseQueryTime` in `useDataSyncStore`. Settings already shows time since last sync, but menu and location screens don't, and there's no offline indicator.

## Scope
- **Offline banner**: "You're offline. Showing menus from 9:42 AM." when the device has no connection.
- **Stale banner**: when the last successful sync is older than a threshold (for example 6 hours) or the cached menu is for an earlier date than today in Central time, show "Menus may be out of date · Last updated yesterday 8:15 PM · Retry".
- **Retry** triggers a sync; on success the banner disappears.
- A subtle "Updated 5 min ago" footer under menus when everything is fresh (optional).

## Technical notes
- Connectivity: `@react-native-community/netinfo` (or `expo-network`).
- The date check matters more than the timestamp: a sync at 11:58 PM is "recent" but its menu is for the wrong day after midnight. Compare the cached menu date with today in Central time.
- Record failed sync attempts too, so the banner can say "Couldn't update" instead of only showing age.
- One shared `<SyncStatusBanner>` component used on Home, location menus and search.
- QA: add "Simulate offline" and "Pretend last sync was yesterday" toggles to the QA menu.

## Done when
- Offline and stale states each show a banner with the last update time and a retry.
- After midnight, a cached menu from yesterday is flagged even if the sync was recent.

issues.body:
Let people set their allergies and dietary needs once, then warn them on any dish anywhere in the app.

## Today

issues.title: Track Dine In Dollars balance and spending pace
issues.body:
Help people track their Dine In Dollars balance and whether they're on pace to make it through the semester.

## Background
Bevo Pay was decommissioned in August 2026. Meal plans now come with **Dine In Dollars**: residence hall plans include $400 per term (Flex plan $1,850 per term), commuter plans include $25 to $100, and faculty and staff can load their own. They work at UHD-run restaurants, coffee shops and markets, roll over, and expire at the end of the spring term (spring 2027 this year).

UT shows the balance and transactions only in UT Direct (https://utdirect.utexas.edu/utapps/uhd/services/dining/transactions/), behind EID + Duo sign-in. There's no public API, and scraping a user's UT Direct session from the app would mean handling their EID credentials, which is a security and App Store risk. So the app can't read the balance automatically.

## Scope (manual MVP)
- Pick your plan (Resident, Flex, Longhorn 25/60/Unlimited, Faculty/Staff, or custom amount) and enter your current balance.
- Quick "log a purchase" from a location page, and an "update balance" field for when you check UT Direct.
- Pace view: "$212 left, 9 weeks to go: about $23/week". Green/amber/red against an even spend line to the end of term, accounting for breaks.
- Link out to UT Direct to check the real balance.
- Optional reminder near end of term: "You have $60 that expires on May 15".
- Everything stays on the device.

## Technical notes
- Store in local SQLite (new `dining_dollars_entries` table: amount, kind purchase/adjustment, date, location id).
- Plan amounts and term dates change every year, so keep them in Supabase (`meal_plans` table or `app_information`), editable in the dashboard, not hard-coded.
- Hide or label locations in the app that accept Dine In Dollars (`methods_of_payment` already exists per location; add a Dine In Dollars value if it's missing).
- Later: ask UHD if a read-only balance API or a shareable export exists. If it ever does, replace manual entry.

## Done when
- A user can set a plan and balance, log spending, and see whether they're on pace.
- Plan amounts and term dates come from Supabase.


## Feasibility of automatic balance
Researched 2026-11-27. Short version: there's no API we can use today, and UT sign-in alone wouldn't give us the balance. The realistic path is manual entry plus a link to the GET app, with a request to Housing and Dining for a read-only balance feed.

### What UT actually runs
- The card system behind Dine In Dollars is **CBORD GET** (CBORD and Transact have merged, now rebranding as Illumia). UT has a live GET portal at [get.cbord.com/utaustin](https://get.cbord.com/utaustin/full/about.php), contact Housing and Dining (uhd.get@austin.utexas.edu, 512-471-6318). Its login redirects to UT's own SAML sign-in at enterprise.login.utexas.edu.
- UT's [Order Food Ahead](https://housing.utexas.edu/dining/dining-services/order-food-ahead) page tells students to download the [GET Mobile](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/get-mobile/id844091049) app, choose UT Austin, and sign in with their EID to connect their Dine In Dollars. So **an official app already shows the balance**: GET Mobile.
- UT Direct also shows balance and history ([faculty/staff page](https://housing.utexas.edu/dining/meal-plans/faculty-staff-dine-dollars) links to utdirect.utexas.edu/utapps/uhd/services/dining/dollars/).
- UT's digital ID in Apple Wallet starts with the fall 2027 class ([UT News](https://news.utexas.edu/2026/03/23/tap-in-ut-to-go-digital-with-university-ids/)). Wallet student IDs can show balances, but third-party apps can't read Wallet pass data, so this doesn't help us.

### Options
| Option | What it needs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Manual entry + "Open GET" button** (current MVP) | Nothing from UT. Deep link / App Store link to GET Mobile and UT Direct so checking the real balance is one tap. | **Do this now.** |
| **2. Official balance feed from Housing and Dining** | UHD (the GET system owner) agrees to expose a read-only balance per student, e.g. via CBORD/Transact's partner APIs ([partner program](https://careers.transactcampus.com/company/partners), [Campus ID News on open APIs](`` https://www.campusidnews.com/transacts-data-aggregation-platform-set-to-expand-into-campus-commerce-and-id-space ``)). Needs a sponsoring UT department, a written data agreement (FERPA), likely CBORD/Illumia partner onboarding, and student consent. | Long shot but the only legitimate automatic route. **Worth an email to UHD.** |
| **3. "Sign in with UT EID" in our app** | UT Enterprise Authentication supports SAML 2.0 and, since Dec 2025, OIDC ([IAM announcement](https://iamservices.utexas.edu/?p=7363)). But it is only for "campus departments and their duly sponsored third-party service providers" ([Authentication AUP](https://iamservices.utexas.edu/resources/policies/authentication-acceptable-use-policy/)); the department is liable for the provider and a data agreement is expected ([vendor requirements](https://iamservices.utexas.edu/resources/vendor-guide-to-iam-at-ut/vendor-requirements/), [cloud integration guidelines](https://tech.utexas.edu/sites/default/files/documents/iam-cloud-integration-guidelines.pdf)). A student project can't register on its own. | **Doesn't solve the problem by itself.** SSO only proves who the user is (EID, name, affiliation). It gives no access to GET or UT Direct data. Only useful combined with option 2. |
| **4. Reverse-engineered GET API** | An unofficial wrapper exists ([cbord-getservices-api-docs](https://cbord-getservices-api-docs.pages.dev), not affiliated with CBORD). It needs the user's GET session, which means running UT's login inside our app and capturing the session. | **Ruled out.** Undocumented, can break anytime, likely against CBORD's terms, and the AUP prohibits "attempts to circumvent centralized authentication services." It also puts a student's whole card account (spending, door access) in our hands. |
| **5. Ask for EID password / scrape UT Direct** | Students type their EID + password into our app, we log in for them. | **Ruled out.** Collecting EID passwords is a security and policy problem (Duo bypass attempts, AUP, App Store review, liability if leaked). We won't do this. |
| **6. Import from an export** | GET Mobile and UT Direct don't offer a CSV/shareable export that we could find. | Not available. Revisit if UHD adds one. |

### How GET Mobile gets the balance (confirmed by Ethan 2026-11-27: it shows Dine In Dollars)
- GET is CBORD's own front end for the card system UT bought from CBORD. The balances live in UT's CBORD card system (CS Gold or Odyssey; GET "seamlessly integrates with both", per [Campus ID News](https://www.campusidnews.com/news-item/get-cbord-student-modern-mobile-experience-modern-student)). UT pays for GET as an add-on subscription, and UT Housing and Dining runs it.
- Sign-in goes through UT's own Enterprise Authentication (the GET login redirects to enterprise.login.utexas.edu). UT has set up GET as a trusted service, so after you sign in, CBORD's servers look up your account in UT's card system and return your balance.
- So GET doesn't have special access to *you*. It has access because **UT made CBORD its card vendor and turned GET on**. A third party would need the same thing: UT agreeing to it.

### Official ways a third party could get the same data
- **Illumia (Transact + CBORD) partner program.** Transact and CBORD rebranded as [Illumia](``` https://www.campusidnews.com/transact-cbord-officially-becomes-illumia-announces-2026-distinction-award-winners/ ```) in March 2026. It has 300+ [technology partners](https://illumiatech.com/partners) that integrate "through open APIs". CBORD also has a Commerce API that covers CS Gold, GET and Odyssey ([support article](https://support.cbord.com/hc/en-us/articles/32999790729755-CBORD-Commerce-API-Documentation), needs a login to read). None of this is public self-serve. Partners are companies with contracts, and each campus has to turn the integration on.
- **How others did it.** Every official case found is a business the school enabled, not a student app: Grubhub Campus and BYPPOCAMPUS take meal plan and dining dollar payments through Transact/CBORD integrations ([Grubhub integration overview](https://grubhubforcampusguides.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411849402772-System-Overview-Campus-Card-Integration-System-Diagrams), [BYPPO](https://www.byppo.com/post/redefining-campus-dining-through-campus-meal-plan-integration)). A Tacit help article says balance access needs "additional API's to be provided by the school" ([Tacit](https://maegan.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/5837967338893-Which-payment-programs-does-Tacit-integrate-with)). I found no student-built app with an official balance integration.
- **What UT could do.** UHD owns the card system, so it could (a) ask CBORD/Illumia to enable a read-only balance integration for UT Dining, or (b) build a small read-only endpoint that returns the signed-in student's balance, and sponsor UT Dining's EID sign-in (OIDC) so only that student can call it. Both need UHD to want it, a sponsoring department, a FERPA data agreement, and probably a security review by UT's ISO.

So the answer to "how does GET do it" is: it's UT's vendor, inside UT's system. The only clean way for us is through UHD.

### Recommendation
1. Ship the manual MVP, and make "Check real balance" open the GET Mobile app (fallback: App Store link, then UT Direct). This is most of the value with zero risk.
2. Ethan emails UHD (uhd.get@austin.utexas.edu) asking whether a read-only Dine In Dollars balance could be shared with UT Dining via CBORD/Transact, and whether UHD would sponsor an Enterprise Authentication (OIDC) integration. If they say yes, options 2 + 3 together give real automatic balances.
3. Don't build options 4 or 5.

issues.title: Let people rate dishes and show top rated today

labels.name: backend
labels.description: Supabase, edge functions, scraper or shared DB package

issues.body:
Let people rate dishes and surface what's good today.

## Scope
- Thumbs up / thumbs down on each menu item (food detail screen, and maybe a swipe action).
- Show a percentage and count, for example "86% liked · 142 ratings", only once an item has enough ratings (for example 10+).
- "Top rated today" section per hall, built from today's menu and all-time ratings.
- One rating per device per item. Changing your rating replaces the old one.
- No written reviews for now (avoids moderation).

## Technical notes
- Identity: the app has no user accounts. Options:
  - **Anonymous device id** (the same `device_id` used in `user_devices`). Simplest, but anyone can reinstall or script requests to stuff votes.
  - **Supabase anonymous sign-in**. Gives each install a real auth uid for RLS, still no login screen. Recommended.
  - Optionally verify with App Attest / DeviceCheck later if abuse shows up.
- Tables: `dish_ratings` (food key, location, user id, value ±1, updated_at), unique on (food key, user id). RLS: a user can insert/update/delete only their own rows. A view or RPC returns aggregated counts so raw votes aren't readable.
- Food key: menu items have no stable id across days. Use a normalized name (plus location or not, decide whether "Mac and Cheese" at J2 and at JCL is the same dish). The same key problem applies to favorite alerts.
- Abuse limits: rate-limit writes per user, and ignore ratings from accounts that rate hundreds of items in minutes.
- Sync aggregated scores into the app's local cache with the menu sync so the UI stays offline-friendly.
- Dashboard: a simple list of most and least liked dishes would be useful for spotting data problems, and could be shared with UHD.
- Privacy policy: mention that ratings are stored with an anonymous id.

## Done when
- A rating can be set and changed, and persists across app restarts.
- Scores appear only above the minimum count.
- "Top rated today" shows for each hall that has a menu today.

issues.title: Show crowd levels and wait times for dining halls

labels.name: backend
labels.description: Supabase, edge functions, scraper or shared DB package

issues.body:
Show how busy each dining hall is right now and the likely wait, for example "J2 · Busy · ~10 min line", plus a "usually busy at" chart by hour.

## Feasibility

UT doesn't publish occupancy data, so the core question is where the numbers come from. Possible sources:

| Source | How it works | Accuracy | Cold start | Privacy / App Store | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Crowdsourced reports** | Users tap "Not busy / Busy / Packed" (and maybe line length) when at a hall | Good when recent reports exist, nothing otherwise | Bad: needs many active users at each hall at the same time. Most of the day there will be no recent report | Low risk. Anonymous device id, no location needed. Needs abuse limits (rate limit per device, drop outliers) | Small Supabase table, free tier |
| **App-open / location pings near halls** | Count devices that open the app while inside a hall's geofence | Weak: only counts app users, who are a small and skewed share of diners. Works as a relative signal (busier than usual) | Needs enough users with location on | Highest risk. Requires location permission with a clear purpose string, a privacy policy update and App Store privacy labels ("Location: used for app functionality"). Background location would likely be rejected, so foreground only | Low |
| **Swipe / transaction counts from UT** | UHD meal-swipe turnstile or POS counts per hall, every few minutes | Best possible: real entries | None | Fine if aggregated by UT | Free if UT agrees, but needs a contact in University Housing and Dining and probably a data agreement. Unknown whether they'd share. Long lead time |
| **Google Popular Times** | Google's busyness by hour and "live" busyness | Decent for typical hours, live data is patchy for campus buildings | None for typical hours | No official API. Scraping breaks Google's terms and is fragile. Not recommended | Free but unsupported |
| **Campus Wi-Fi device counts** | Connected devices per access point near each hall | Good relative signal | None | Aggregated counts only, but it's UT ITS data, so same access problem as swipe counts | Needs UT ITS cooperation |

Other notes:
- **Wait time** is harder than busyness. Without real counts, it can only be estimated from crowdsourced reports ("line about 10 min").
- **Typical hours** (a "usually busy" chart) are much easier than live data: a fixed curve per hall and meal, seeded from staff knowledge or a few weeks of reports, would be useful even with no live data at all.
- Every live number needs a "last updated" time, and should hide itself when data is stale (for example older than 20 minutes) rather than show a guess.

## Recommended MVP
1. Ship a **"Usually busy" chart** per dining hall from a hand-built baseline (per hall, per meal, per weekday), editable in the dashboard. No new permissions.
2. Add **one-tap crowdsourced reports** ("How busy is it?") shown only on a hall's page during open hours, displayed only when there are recent reports. Store anonymous reports in Supabase with a per-device rate limit.
3. In parallel, **ask UHD** whether they can share aggregate swipe counts. If they say yes, replace both with real data.

Skip location pings and Google Popular Times for now: the privacy and terms cost outweighs the accuracy they'd add.

## Technical notes
- New Supabase table `crowd_reports` (location_id, level enum, optional wait minutes, device_id, created_at) with insert-only RLS for anon and a rate limit (Edge Function or a check constraint via a function).
- Aggregate with a view or RPC that returns the latest level per hall over the last 20 minutes, weighted by recency.
- Baseline curves in a `location_busyness_baseline` table, editable from the dashboard.
- Times in Central time.
- Privacy policy and App Store privacy labels need updating only if location is ever used.

## Done when
- Each dining hall shows a "usually busy" chart.
- Users can submit a busyness report, and recent reports show with their age, hidden when stale.

issues.title: Notify when a favorited dish is on today's menu
issues.body:
Notify people when a dish they favorited is on today's menu, for example "Queso Mac is at J2 for lunch today".

## Scope
- Opt-in setting: "Favorite alerts", off by default, with a time to be notified (default around 9 AM Central).
- One digest notification per day, not one per dish: "3 of your favorites are on today's menus". Tapping opens a list of them with location and meal.
- Per-location filter (only alert for halls I use) as a follow-up.
- No notification on days when none of your favorites are served.

## Technical notes
Favorites live only on the device today (the `favorites` table in the app's SQLite, `apps/mobile/services/database/favorites.ts`), and push tokens are in `user_devices` keyed by `device_id`. Two ways to do this:

1. **On-device (recommended for MVP)**: a background task (`expo-background-task`) syncs today's menus and schedules a local notification if favorites match. No server changes and favorites stay private. Downside: iOS decides when background tasks run, so delivery time isn't guaranteed and won't happen if the app was force-quit.
2. **Server push**: upload favorites per device to a new Supabase table (`device_favorites`: device_id, food name, location name), and after the scraper's daily run an Edge Function matches them against menus and sends pushes through the existing helper in `supabase/functions/_shared/push.ts`. Reliable timing, but stores favorites server-side, so the privacy policy needs a line and RLS must stop devices reading each other's rows.

Start with option 1 and move to option 2 if delivery is too unreliable.

- Match on the same name + location key the app already uses. Menu names change slightly between days, so consider a normalized name.
- Respect the existing notification permission flow (`usePermission`, onboarding `PermissionsScreen`).

## Done when
- With alerts on and a favorite on today's menu, one notification arrives that day and opens the matching list.
- No notification on days with no matches.

## Expo packages
- **`expo-notifications`** (already installed, `~58.1.6`, used today only for push registration in `services/notifications/notifications.ts`): use `Notifications.scheduleNotificationAsync()` with a date trigger for the daily digest. The app already knows the next few days of menus after a sync, so it can schedule the matching digests ahead of time (cancel and reschedule after each sync with `cancelScheduledNotificationAsync`). That works even if iOS never runs a background task, and costs nothing on the server.
- **`expo-background-task`** (`~58.0.13`, not installed): optional, to refresh menus and reschedule while the app isn't opened for a few days.
- Tapping the notification should deep link through the existing response listener in `notifications.ts`.

issues.title: Add Live Activities for closing time and current meal
issues.body:
Use iOS Live Activities to show time-sensitive dining info on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island.

Follows on from #111 (widgets), which lists a closing-time Live Activity as a maybe-later item. This issue now owns that.

## Ideas
- **Closing countdown**: start from a location's page ("Track until close"). Shows open/closed, a countdown to closing, and the next opening time once closed.
- **Current meal at a favorite hall**: shows the current meal period (breakfast, lunch, dinner) and a few items, switching when the meal changes.
- Optional: start automatically when you open a hall's menu shortly before it closes (opt-in setting).

## Technical notes
- Needs a widget extension with an `ActivityConfiguration` (lock screen view plus compact, minimal and expanded Dynamic Island views). It should share the extension and config plugin from #111, so build that first or together.
- Start, update and end from JS through a small native module (or a maintained Expo Live Activity library).
- Countdowns use `Text(timerInterval:)` so they tick without updates. Meal changes are known ahead of time, so the app can set the state at start and schedule an end date; no server needed for the MVP.
- Remote updates (ActivityKit push tokens through APNs) would only be needed if menus or hours change mid-activity. Out of scope for the MVP.
- Times in Central time (`America/Chicago`). Activities end automatically at most 8 hours after start (iOS limit), so end at closing time.
- Needs `NSSupportsLiveActivities` in Info.plist and an EAS build (no OTA).

## Done when
- A closing countdown can be started from a location and ends at closing time.
- Lock screen and Dynamic Island views look right in light and dark mode.

## Expo packages
- **`expo-widgets`** (SDK 58, `~58.0.30`, first-party): also covers Live Activities. Define the views in React with `createLiveActivity()` (lock screen plus compact, minimal and expanded Dynamic Island layouts) and start, update and end them from JS, so no custom native module is needed. It also exposes push-to-start and push tokens (`addPushToStartTokenListener`) if remote updates are ever added. Recommended, and it shares the setup with #111.
- **`@expo/ui`** (`~58.0.30`): the SwiftUI components the activity views are built from.
- **`@bacons/apple-targets`**: fallback for a hand-written SwiftUI `ActivityConfiguration` if `expo-widgets` falls short.
- Not installed today. Needs an EAS build, not OTA.

issues.title: Add iOS home screen and lock screen widgets
issues.body:
Add iOS widgets so people can check dining hours and menus without opening the app.

## Ideas

**Home screen widgets**
- **Open now**: favorite (or nearby) locations that are open, with closing times. Small and medium sizes.
- **Current meal**: what a favorite hall is serving for the current meal (breakfast, lunch or dinner), a few items with a "more in app" tap target.
- **Favorites today**: favorited menu items being served today, and where.

**Lock screen widgets**
- Compact open/closed status for one chosen location (circular or rectangular accessory), for example "J2 · open until 8 PM".

**Maybe later**
- Live Activities (closing countdown, current meal) moved to #113.

## Technical notes
- The app is Expo SDK 58, so this needs a native WidgetKit extension added through a config plugin (for example `@bacons/apple-targets` or a custom plugin), written in SwiftUI.
- Share data with the extension through an App Group: either the cached SQLite database or a small JSON snapshot the app writes after each sync (likely simpler). Reload timelines with `WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines()` after a sync.
- Hours must be computed in Central time (`America/Chicago`), not the device time zone.
- Timeline entries should flip at each opening and closing boundary so status stays correct without the app running.
- Widget configuration (which location) via `AppIntentConfiguration`, using the app's location list.
- Deep links from each widget into the matching location or menu screen.
- Needs an EAS build (not OTA) to ship, and new App Store screenshots once it lands.

## Done when
- At least one home screen widget and one lock screen widget ship in a TestFlight build.
- Statuses and times match the app, in Central time, including closed days.
- Tapping a widget opens the right screen.

## Expo packages
- **`expo-widgets`** (SDK 58, `~58.0.30`, first-party): build the widgets in React with `createWidget()` and `@expo/ui` SwiftUI components instead of writing a Swift extension by hand. Its config plugin adds the WidgetKit target and App Group. Push new data with `widget.updateTimeline()` / `after(date)` entries after each menu sync, so open/closed flips at each boundary. This is the recommended path.
- **`@expo/ui`** (`~58.0.30`): required by `expo-widgets` for the widget views (`Text`, `HStack`, `Image` with SF Symbols, etc.).
- **`@bacons/apple-targets`** (v5, supports Expo 52+): fallback if `expo-widgets` can't do something we need (for example `AppIntentConfiguration` for picking a location). It generates a plain SwiftUI widget target from `targets/widget/` and keeps it out of `ios/` so prebuild stays clean.
- Neither is installed today. Both need an EAS build, not OTA.

issues.title: 2.0.0 cutover: steps after merging staging into main
issues.body:
Steps for **after** the `staging` to `main` promotion PR is merged. The pre-merge steps (prod migrations, the 2.0.0 App Store release, the website move) stay in #25.

## Same session as the merge

- [ ] Check what started automatically: CI on `main`, the Vercel production builds of `apps/dashboard` and `apps/website`, the `Scrape menus` schedule (07:00 UTC, prod), the dev keepalive, and the `Scrape menus (dev)` daily run.
- [ ] **Dashboard sign-in (#46):** turn **Email** off in prod Supabase, Authentication, Providers. Google is already on.
- [ ] `supabase functions deploy manual-push-notification` against prod, from `main`. This one deploy carries #46 (admin-only), #51 (service-role bearer for the CLI) and #54 (`sb_secret_` keys, `verify_jwt = false` from `supabase/config.toml`). Then check three things: an anon call gets 403, a Google admin session can send a test push to your own phone, and `pnpm -s admin notifications send` works with `--prod` (preview first).
- [ ] Sign in to `https://dashboard.utdining.app` with Google as `ethanlanting@gmail.com`. Check that one write works, for example saving configuration without changes.
- [ ] Delete the downloaded `client_secret_*.json` from `~/Downloads`.
- [ ] Optional: delete the old email/password dashboard user in Authentication, Users.
- Rollback: turn Email back on and re-deploy the previous `manual-push-notification`. To restore the old write rules, re-run `alter policy ... to authenticated using (true) with check (true)` for the policies the allowlist migration changed.

## Scraper: Render to GitHub Actions (#9)

- [ ] **Same day, before the next 07:00 UTC:** suspend the Render cron `ut-dining-scraper-new`. Don't delete it. If both run, they write to prod at the same time.
- [ ] Run `Scrape menus` once by hand from the Actions tab (blank input uses `DAYS_TO_SCRAPE`). Check the log, including the "Removed N stale menus" lines, and that the app shows today's menus.
- [ ] Check the next scheduled 07:00 UTC run, then close #9 by hand.
- Rollback: resume the Render cron and disable `Scrape menus` in the Actions tab.

## Dashboard and status page

- [ ] The first `main` build of `ut-dining-dashboard` becomes production. Check that it's READY and built from the merge commit, then view locations, notifications and configuration.
- [ ] `https://status.utdining.app/api/status` answers 200 with JSON. Today it redirects (307) because production still runs the old dashboard.
- [ ] EthanL06/ut-dining-uptime#1 should close on its own once `/api/status` is live. If it doesn't within a day, check the Upptime workflow.
- Rollback: Vercel instant rollback to `dpl_GToJvNJGJZUwTqTpfqVjCuUskrW3`. After the allowlist migration that old dashboard is read-only.

## Website

- [ ] The first `main` build of `ut-dining-website` replaces the manual production deploy from #47's branch. Check that `https://utdining.app`, `/changelog/` and `/privacy-policy/` load.

## Lock down `main`

- [ ] Once `mobile-e2e.yml` is on `main`, add "Maestro on iOS" and "Lint, typecheck, test" as required status checks in the "Protect main" ruleset (Settings, Rules, Rulesets). The cloud proxy blocks ruleset writes, so this one is yours.
- [ ] Install the Renovate GitHub app (after main has the config): https://github.com/apps/renovate, this repo only. Renovate reads `renovate.json` from `main` (#78).
- [ ] Turn on Dependabot alerts (leave Dependabot security updates off): https://github.com/EthanL06/UT-Dining/settings/security_analysis (#78).
- Note: `main` requires a PR for every change, so later fixes go through `staging` and the next promotion PR.

## After 2.0.0 is live in the App Store

- [ ] Set `release_date` on the `2.0.0` row of `changelog` in prod (CLI: `pnpm -s admin changelog ... --prod`, dry run first).
- [ ] Optional: set `app_information.app_version` to `2.0.0` so older installs get the forced update.
- [ ] Replace the old Pages site with redirect pages to `utdining.app`, then the repo cleanup PR: drop `WEBSITE_STATIC_EXPORT`, the `/ut-dining-website` base path and `website-deploy.yml`, and update `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/cook.md`, `README.md`, the e2e fixture and `supabase/seed.sql`.

## After a week of clean runs

- [ ] Delete the Render cron, then archive `EthanL06/ut-dining-scraper` and `EthanL06/ut-dining-dashboard`.
- [ ] Delete merged branches.

head_commit.message:
feat(mobile): native header and in-page search on dining hall menus (#172)

Dining hall menus use the native iOS header with a large title and header buttons. The menu search field moves into the page so it zooms with it, and there are glass scroll to top and search buttons. Fixes #164.

Fixes the header disappearing or flickering after a cancelled half swipe back on zoom-opened menus, Favorites and Meal Plan. This is a react-native-screens patch that restores the bar after a cancel and keeps it shown for 2 s. The root patches folder is now part of the app fingerprint.
